You can see our little, lots of little up arrows on our stats. Let's see. Even during the shutdown, the library was able to do curbside delivery. We call it porch pickup for our users. And we were also able to offer through Zoom a virtual meeting space for community groups because we had a subscription. It didn't sort of end after 40 minutes. And so several groups used that. And then towards the end of the year, we were pleased to be able to start hosting meetings again. And I hear a lot of little comments from people about how much they appreciated our various services during the pandemic. But we were excited to get back in the library or beside the library, particularly our children's programs. We wanted to bring back, we had outdoor story time. We also started a beginner French program because we had a French-speaking co-op student. And that was very popular. It started online, it shifted to in-person. And we did our summer program. It was mostly take-home crafts and one online workshop, but we were able to have one in-person outdoor workshop. And because a lot of the program is the prize draw, which is extremely popular, kids were able to come in and get books and put in their tickets and all of that. So that was a happy thing. We were also pleased with so many things being cut off that we were able to partner with some of our groups. We started the seed library with Sustainable Miracle Wolford. That one got in just during that little open period in the early spring, and then we got shut down again, but we put it online and that cart is on wheels. So we were able to take it outside and for people to pick out seeds. And we also were involved with the Echo Champions Contest, which is an environmental contest being started locally. And we continue to work with Trails Group on Story Trail and their new Riverwalk Trail, which is right beside where the library is. And we'd like to thank the Lions Club for donating for all of these projects. And while we're expressing appreciation, the province continues to fund internet, our interlibrary loan postage and just the regular operating grant. We'd like to thank our donors. Our volunteers all came back when we reopened, so we were excited about that. And someone donated a tiny door to us, which was very pleasing. Behind the scenes, the library upgraded our catalog and circulation system to a better one that's more high-end, but it's part of a consortium, so it's more affordable.
